name: Notations Ecosystem Control Plane
description: The private coordination backend of the Notations Universe: an append-only, SHA-256 hash-linked and Ed25519-signed journal of node registrations, relations, health observations, security posture and capability requests. Credentials resolve to principals whose roles decide what they may do and which actor identity they may record, so the audit trail is authenticated rather than self-asserted. It records intent and operator approval but never stores provider credentials, key material, vulnerability detail or network topology, and never dispatches an external call.

capabilities.label: Read the ecosystem snapshot
capabilities.description: GET /v1/snapshot: current nodes (with derived health), relations, coordination records, revision and event cursor.
capabilities.provenance: the append-only journal, folded; nothing is fetched to answer

capabilities.label: Read events after a cursor
capabilities.description: GET /v1/events?after=<eventCursor>&limit=<n>: append-only records after a known cursor, paginated with a server-side cap; 409 CURSOR_UNKNOWN means refresh the snapshot.

capabilities.label: Liveness and journal summary
capabilities.description: GET /health (unauthenticated): liveness and uptime only. It deliberately discloses no revision and no node count, so an anonymous caller learns nothing about history.
capabilities.provenance: the journal head and this process; no node is contacted

capabilities.label: Register or revise a node
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=register_node with expectedRevision. Declares a node's kind, capabilities (observe/propose/execute), bounded metadata and optional location.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own command, validated at the write boundary

capabilities.label: Declare a relation between nodes
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=declare_relation: supplies_context_to, coordinates, visualizes, governs or depends_on between two registered nodes.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own command, validated at the write boundary

capabilities.label: Record a health observation
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=record_observation from an operator, health check or webhook; derives the node's health in the snapshot.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own observation; the plane probes nothing itself

capabilities.label: Request a capability of another node
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=request_capability: a reasoning engine or dock states intent to use a target capability in its declared mode; execute intents become approval_required and stay dispatch=not_dispatched.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own request; approval is not execution

capabilities.label: Approve or reject a coordination request
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=resolve_coordination by an operator. Separation of duties: the approving actor may not be the actor that proposed the intent. Approval is not execution: the record stays not_dispatched.
capabilities.provenance: an operator decision, attributed to a bound actor

capabilities.label: Read the control plane's own security posture
capabilities.description: GET /v1/security/status: identity binding, the authorization model, transport state, key lifecycle, journal integrity and abuse counters. Requires the operator or admin role. Names no credential, key, address or journal content.
capabilities.provenance: this process: configuration, journal state and rate-limit counters

capabilities.label: Record a security posture attestation
capabilities.description: POST /v1/commands action=record_security_posture: up to 12 signals across identity, authorization, encryption, key lifecycle, dependency risk, exposure, audit integrity, backup, incident and control-plane integrity. Carries states, coverage fractions and severity counts only.
capabilities.provenance: an attestor's signals, past the evidence boundary that strips the material

capabilities.label: Issue a principal credential
capabilities.description: CLI: mints an ncp.<keyId>.<secret> credential bound to a principal, its roles, the actor identities it may claim and optionally the nodes it may act for. The secret is printed once; only a SHA-256 digest is stored.
capabilities.provenance: generated here; the registry keeps only the SHA-256 digest

capabilities.label: Rotate the journal signing key
capabilities.description: CLI: generates a new Ed25519 signing key, retires the previous one and records the journal length from which the new key is expected. Records signed by the retired key keep verifying.
capabilities.provenance: generated here; the private half never leaves the key store

capabilities.label: Verify a journal replica offline
capabilities.description: `node control-plane/src/security/cli.js verify <journal>` reads, verifies and reports — chain, signature coverage, anchor agreement and a breakdown by event kind — writing nothing. After an integrity alarm an operator must be able to ask 'is this replica sound?' without starting a server against it, because starting one would append to a history that may be wrong.
capabilities.provenance: a journal replica on disk, checked against the anchor

capabilities.label: Read the plane's own posture
capabilities.description: GET /v1/security/status: identity binding, the authorization model, transport state, key lifecycle, journal integrity and abuse counters. Requires security.status.read. It names no credential, no key, no address and no journal content.

relations.description: Confirmed by code: the control plane's OpenAPI contract and validation.js are the only contract the dock follows. dock/src/api/controlPlane.ts consumes /v1/snapshot, /v1/events and /v1/commands exactly as specified, dock/src/control-plane.d.ts types the snapshot, and the console lens validates every drafted command with the control plane's own validator before submitting it with expectedRevision.

contracts.name: OpenAPI
contracts.summary: Five routes, 25 stable error codes, and the coordination record whose `dispatch` is a const: approval is not execution, stated where a client can read it.

contracts.name: journal record
contracts.summary: event + previousHash + recordHash + optional signature, and nothing else: a field outside that set is covered by neither the hash nor the signature and is refused.

contracts.name: identity space
contracts.summary: notation://<class>/<namespace>/<local-id>[@version], eighteen classes in an information family and an authority family. resolve() throws by construction.

contracts.name: corpus doctrine
contracts.summary: Ten invariants, five roles, four standings. Graded by ecosystem/corpus.mjs and carried into the snapshot as derived node metadata.

resources.name: coordination journal
resources.description: Append-only, SHA-256 hash-linked and Ed25519-signed. Holds node registrations, relations, health observations, security posture and coordination records, and nothing above INTERNAL.

resources.name: rollback anchor
resources.description: Head hash and length, written after each durable append. A truncated journal still verifies as a chain; only the anchor catches it.

resources.name: signing key store
resources.description: Public verification material for every key ever active, and the active private half wrapped by envelope encryption under CONTROL_PLANE_KEK. Gitignored, mode 0600.

resources.name: credential registry
resources.description: SHA-256 digests, roles, actor and node bindings. Holds no usable credential: a stolen registry yields nothing to authenticate with.

environment.name: NOTATIONS_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN
environment.purpose: The operator bearer the seed tool and the dock present; the plane stores only its SHA-256 digest.

environment.name: CONTROL_PLANE_KEK
environment.purpose: The key-encryption key the journal signing key is envelope-encrypted under. Never written by this repository and never returned in a response.

reference.spatial: Carries node locations declared at registration; has no location of its own.
reference.temporal: Every record has recordedAt; observations carry observedAt; snapshot carries generatedAt and a revision.
open_questions: Which execution adapters will sit behind approved intents, and where will they run?

A corpus conformance producer, shaped like security/attest.mjs but running inside each system, is what would move a corpus grade from declared to measured. Today 90 of 117 evidence paths point into repositories this one cannot open.
The rollback anchor is not off-host replication: an attacker who rewrites journal and anchor together defeats it. `backup` posture reports unknown until a replica is configured.

corpus.holding: The coordination journal of the universe: node registrations, relations, health observations, security posture and capability requests, as an append-only hash-linked and signed chain.

COR-001.note: The journal is the holding, and its extent is the five record kinds the contract admits.

COR-002.note: Coordinates between canonical states without owning any domain's. The journal is its own record, not a domain's state.

COR-003.note: Records that a system exists and what it may do; it holds no domain values to carry a basis.

COR-004.note: Records recordedAt and observedAt for its own events; it holds no domain values whose knowability could differ from their occurrence.

COR-005.note: Every refusal is typed with a code, a detail and a remedy, and an unknown action acquires no default semantics.

COR-006.note: Admits no evidence into a canonical state; it records intent and approval, and dispatches nothing.

COR-007.note: Holds no raw material: source artifacts, documents and datasets are refused at the boundary by construction.

COR-008.note: SHA-256 hash-linked, Ed25519-signed, with a rollback anchor that makes truncation loud.

COR-009.note: Approval is not execution: every coordination record stays not_dispatched and the plane never calls outward.

COR-010.note: Names what it must never hold — credentials, key material, vulnerability detail, network topology, offensive capability, pointers to raw findings — and refuses each at the command boundary.
